title: TB pericarditis and steroids
dek: Effusive pericardial TB is extra-pulmonary disease with tamponade risk. Adjuvant steroids are a WHO-conditional, HIV-stratified decision — not a copy-paste from TBM.
story: Tuberculous pericarditis presents as effusion, tamponade, or constriction. Diagnosis is a pericardial fluid WRD/culture/biopsy problem plus the pulmonary workup you must not skip. Treat as TB disease with a full regimen; TPT has no role once disease is present.

Adjunctive corticosteroids: TBM has a clearer mortality rationale. Pericarditis evidence (including IMPI) is mixed and HIV-stratified — steroids may reduce constriction in some HIV-negative patients and have not been a free lunch in HIV-positive pericarditis. Follow the current WHO extra-pulmonary overlay, not a TBM protocol copied onto the pericardium.
Tamponade is drainage, not a molecular DST delay. Constriction is surgery in selected chronic cases. Rifamycins still induce the steroid you just started — dose accordingly.
deep: Ultra on pericardial fluid: useful when positive; negative does not exclude.
Adenosine deaminase in fluid is an adjunct, not a WRD.
Do not withhold pericardiocentesis for a “better specimen tomorrow” if the blood pressure is disappearing.
Pregnancy plus tamponade is two emergencies.

visual.caption: Pericardial TB: treat disease, drain tamponade, consider steroids as a separate HIV-stratified decision from TBM.

example.setup: CD4 90, pericardial TB likely, no neurologic signs. Team copies TBM steroid taper.

steps.title: Treat the TB
steps.body: HRZE or the correct DR regimen. That is not optional.

steps.title: Steroids are a pericarditis-specific, HIV-stratified call
steps.body: IMPI-era caution in HIV+; do not autopilot TBM doses.

steps.title: Watch IRIS and glucose
steps.body: ART timing still follows pulmonary/TBM rules by site of disease.

example.takeaway: Pericardial TB is EPTB with a drainage clock; steroids are not TBM-identical.
